clinicalPearls: A spectrum of skeletal ciliopathies unified by a narrow, long thorax with short horizontal ribs and variable limb shortening
Encompasses Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy and the more severe, often lethal short-rib polydactyly syndromes (Saldino-Noonan, Majewski, Verma-Naumoff and Beemer-Langer types)
Polydactyly is present in some subtypes and absent in others, so its absence does not exclude the diagnosis
Neonatal respiratory insufficiency from a constricted rib cage dominates the early clinical picture
Extra-skeletal involvement includes cystic renal disease, hepatic fibrosis, retinal dystrophy and pancreatic or intestinal anomalies
Caused by biallelic variants in intraflagellar transport and dynein-2 motor genes, most commonly DYNC2H1
Survivors of infancy may later develop progressive renal and hepatic disease requiring surveillance
reference.pathophysiology: The short-rib thoracic dysplasias result from biallelic variants in genes encoding components of the intraflagellar transport system and the cytoplasmic dynein-2 retrograde motor, most often DYNC2H1. These proteins are essential for building and maintaining the primary cilium, through which hedgehog and other signals that pattern the developing skeleton are transduced. Disrupted ciliary signalling in growth-plate chondrocytes impairs endochondral ossification, producing the characteristically short ribs, narrow thorax and shortened limbs, while abnormal hedgehog signalling in the limb bud underlies the polydactyly seen in some subtypes. Because the same cilia are required in kidney, liver, retina and pancreas, affected individuals may also develop cystic kidney disease, hepatic fibrosis, retinal degeneration and other visceral abnormalities.
additionalDifferentials: Thanatophoric dysplasia and other lethal skeletal dysplasias
additionalInvestigations: Skeletal survey to assess rib length, thoracic dimensions, pelvis and limb bones
Chest imaging and respiratory assessment for thoracic insufficiency
Renal ultrasound and renal function testing for cystic or tubulointerstitial disease
Liver function tests and hepatic imaging for fibrosis
Ophthalmological assessment with electroretinography for retinal dystrophy
Molecular testing with a skeletal ciliopathy gene panel
redFlags: Severe thoracic insufficiency and respiratory failure in the newborn
Recurrent respiratory infection with failure to thrive
reference.prognosis: Outcome is highly variable across the spectrum: the lethal short-rib polydactyly forms are fatal in the perinatal period, whereas Jeune syndrome has a variable respiratory course, and survivors of the early years remain at risk of progressive renal and hepatic disease.
pitfalls: Excluding the diagnosis simply because polydactyly is absent
Underestimating the risk of progressive renal or hepatic disease in survivors
Failing to anticipate and plan for a difficult respiratory course
Assuming a uniformly lethal outcome across the whole spectrum
references: GeneReviews: Short-Rib Thoracic Dysplasia with or without Polydactyly
Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: Respiratory support proportionate to thoracic insufficiency, ranging from supplemental oxygen and assisted ventilation to aggressive treatment of recurrent chest infections
Thoracic expansion surgery, such as expansion thoracoplasty or a vertical expandable prosthetic titanium rib, in selected survivable cases to enlarge the constricted rib cage
Surveillance and management of cystic renal disease with monitoring of renal function, treatment of hypertension and renal replacement therapy for progressive failure
Monitoring for hepatic fibrosis with liver function tests and imaging
Ophthalmological surveillance and low-vision support for retinal dystrophy
Coordinated multidisciplinary care across respiratory medicine, thoracic surgery, nephrology, hepatology, ophthalmology and clinical genetics
Genetic counselling with cascade and prenatal testing given autosomal recessive inheritance
